title: TTS Engine Persistence Reversion to Kokoro Across Application Restart
description: Selecting Windows Speech (SAPI5) in Settings appeared to save during the session, but exiting L.U.C.Y. via its Exit control and relaunching reverted the active engine to Kokoro-82M.
evidence: Source code inspection of src/ui/index.html showed settingsTtsEngineSelect statically defaulting to 'kokoro'. Startup config loader failed to set select.value, causing subsequent persistVoiceSettings() calls to overwrite voice-config.json with 'kokoro'. Tests in tests/voice/voice-recovery-execution.test.js pass 8/8.
root_cause: DOM select element was not initialized on startup config load, causing persistVoiceSettings() to read static HTML default ('kokoro') and clobber voice-config.json on disk. Additionally, main/index.js unconditionally pre-warmed Kokoro worker on launch.
user_impact: User preference for lightweight, instant Windows Speech was discarded on application restart, forcing the slow neural model on every fresh boot.
recommended_next_action: Launch the application once with npm start, confirm Windows Speech (SAPI5) is selected in Settings to write the updated setting to AppData disk, and commit working tree fixes.

title: Excessive 22-Second First-Audible Speech Latency and Listening State Deadlock
description: Speech responses took approximately 22 seconds to emit their first audible word, or aborted immediately in 0 ms without producing audio.
evidence: Live Electron A/B benchmark (scratch/verify-live-ab-acceptance.js) measured Kokoro CPU inference at 17,089 ms, while Windows SAPI5 measured 564 ms nominal and 48 ms offline fallback. Source inspection confirmed early return false in _executeSpeech() when isListening was true.
root_cause: Kokoro-82M ONNX model ran on host 15W Intel Core i5-1335U CPU without quantization or GPU acceleration. Additionally, voice-controller.js line 643 aborted speech when isListening was active.
user_impact: Conversational assistant was practically unusable via voice due to multi-second delays or silent failure to respond.
recommended_next_action: Preserve direct SAPI5 routing in voice-controller.js and verified listening state cancellation.

title: Physical Laptop Microphone Wake-Word Rejection and Speaker Feedback Loop
description: Saying 'Hey Lucy' into the physical laptop microphone failed to activate the assistant despite automated synthetic tests reporting success.
evidence: Synthetic tests generated artificial high-frequency noise bursts (hfer > 0.35). Real microphone speech experienced room acoustic attenuation (hfer ~ 0.10-0.15), failing evaluatePhoneticLandmarks sibilant gate (> 0.18). Furthermore, processorNode was connected directly to audioContext.destination, leaking audio to speakers and triggering Windows AEC suppression.
root_cause: Phonetic landmark sibilant gate threshold was excessively high for natural human speech over laptop microphone arrays, and audio recorder lacked a zero-gain isolation node, causing speaker bleed and acoustic echo cancellation suppression.
user_impact: Hands-free voice activation was completely non-functional for real human speakers on laptop hardware.
recommended_next_action: Perform physical microphone acoustic confirmation in a running desktop session with conversational speech.

title: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE Environment Variable Collision in Single-Instance Test
description: Running 'npm run test:flow' in an IDE or terminal session that exports ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 causes tests/flow/single-instance.test.js to fail with exit code 1 instead of 0.
evidence: Executing 'npm run test:flow' failed on single-instance.test.js. Executing 'Remove-Item env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE; node --test tests/flow/single-instance.test.js' passed cleanly with exit code 0.
root_cause: Child Electron process inherits ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE from the parent shell environment, bypassing Electron main process application lifecycle APIs.
user_impact: False negative test failure during flow integration runs when executed from certain IDE shells.
recommended_next_action: Add explicit environment scrubbing (delete process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) in single-instance.test.js before spawning child Electron processes.

title: Ralph CLI Batch Wrapper Label Resolution Failure on Windows cmd.exe
description: Executing 'ralph.cmd status' in Windows cmd.exe returns 'The system cannot find the batch label specified - status'.
evidence: Tested 'ralph.cmd status' via cmd.exe; failed with batch label error. Tested 'powershell -File ralph.ps1 status'; succeeded cleanly with exit code 0.
root_cause: C:\Users\admin\.gemini\bin\ralph.cmd was saved with LF (Unix) line endings instead of CRLF (Windows) line endings, causing cmd.exe label parser to fail to locate :status.
user_impact: Users running cmd.exe cannot use ralph.cmd; must use ralph.ps1 in PowerShell or bash.
recommended_next_action: Convert ralph.cmd line endings from LF to CRLF.

title: Unsigned Windows Packaged Executables Trigger SmartScreen Advisory
description: Production binaries in dist-release are unsigned (Status: NotSigned), triggering Windows Defender SmartScreen unknown publisher advisory upon download.
evidence: Inspected dist-release/L.U.C.Y-Setup-0.1.0-win-x64.exe with PowerShell Get-AuthenticodeSignature; returned NotSigned.
root_cause: Open-source development environment lacks a commercial EV / OV Windows Code Signing Certificate.
user_impact: Users downloading installer binaries from internet browsers see an 'Unknown Publisher' security advisory.
recommended_next_action: Continue providing cryptographic SHA-256 checksums in release-manifest.json and SHA256SUMS.txt; obtain Windows signing certificate if distributing publicly.

title: Portable Distribution NSIS Extraction Collision and Worker Deletion
description: Portable executable failed Step 12 in smoke tests because secondary single-instance extraction deleted LucyUiaWorker.exe out from under running instance.
evidence: scripts/patch-electron-builder.js and unpackDirName: false in electron-builder.yml isolate portable instances in $PLUGINSDIR/app. Verified by tests/packaging/packaging-production.test.js (32/32 pass).
root_cause: Upstream electron-builder logic bug in NsisTarget.js ignored unpackDirName: false; secondary instance RMDir on exit unlinked extracted binaries.
user_impact: Native UI automation crashed with ENOENT in portable distribution runs.
recommended_next_action: Preserve scripts/patch-electron-builder.js postinstall hook in package.json.

title: Missing sql.js WASM Module in Packaged Application ASAR Bundle
description: Installed packaged app crashed on startup with 'Cannot find module sql.js' when initializing memory store.
evidence: electron-builder.yml files glob was updated to include node_modules/sql.js/**/*; dist-release ASAR verified via npx asar list.
root_cause: electron-builder files filter omitted sql.js distribution folder.
user_impact: Packaged release crashed immediately upon attempting SQLite database initialization.

title: External Phone, WhatsApp, and Shopping Capabilities Are Roadmap Placeholders
description: Phone calling, WhatsApp messaging, and shopping workflows are conceptual roadmap features with zero supporting backend code or API integrations.
evidence: Full-codebase grep for 'whatsapp', 'phone', 'shopping' found zero integration modules; only general intent matching for opening installed desktop apps via UIA allowlist.
root_cause: Features were discussed during requirements planning but deferred in favor of core local-first assistant, voice, desktop UIA, and memory continuity capabilities.
user_impact: Users asking Lucy to make phone calls or buy products are routed to general browser or desktop application launch tools.
recommended_next_action: Accurately document these capabilities as planned/unimplemented in user-facing manuals and roadmaps to prevent false expectations.
